newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-MAM full-year profits seen strong.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-MAM full-year profits seen strong.

text.p: British fund manager Mercury Asset Management Plc is likely to show growth of over 20 percent in full-year, pre-tax profits when it reports on Thursday, boosted by growing funds under management and buoyant financial markets.
Analysts said the group had won a number of new mandates and benefited from the unrelenting rise in world equity markets over the year.

They saw pre-tax profits for the year to end-March coming in at between 170 and 175 million sterling against 140.4 million sterling previously. The dividend was seen between 41 and 44.5 pence, up from 29 last year.
MAM reported a 29 percent rise in pre-tax earnings at the half-year stage.

They also said that recent bid talk surrounding the group was unlikely to regain much momentum, the group appearing intent on maintaining its independence following the 1995 demerger from 75 percent owner S.G. Warburg.

MAM announced a 250 million sterling standby loan facility in February, offering a cushion if the group faced a funds crisis similar to the one at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management last year, and signalling that it intends to retain its independence.

Morgan Grenfell parent Deutsche Bank has said it will face a 200 million sterling compensation charge related to the affair, a charge that comes on top of a 180-million pound net injection by the bank to shore up the trusts.
Analysts said the company was on a stronger growth track following a flat performance in the year ended March 31, 1995.

"They had a wobbly patch in performance a couple of years back but it has been put right in the last two years, and is beginning to gain net new mandates. Although not as strong as Schroders, they should have been net gainers to the tune of three, maybe even five billion of new funds," said John Tyce, analyst at SocGen.
MAM said it had gained two billion sterling in net new funds by the half-year stage.

Tyce said the group faced two key challenges in coming months, including the need as chiefly a wholesale operator to tap the retail pension market, which was likely to grow as companies absolved themselves of the responsibility.
Also it needed to grow its international business, an area which Schroders has developed to build funds under management.
"Mercury has done that too but nowhere near as much," said Tyce.
Another analyst said MAM could seek to use its cash pile, at 261.6 million sterling at the half year stage, to fund an acquisition or seek a joint venture either in the U.S. or Europe.

It could seek a fund management acquisition or joint venture in the U.S. or Europe in due course, which the analyst said would be a better use of the cash pile than a distribution to shareholders, given that the positive long-term savings market outlook.
